Two consequences on the server's 20 Hz tick, with 307 monsters in the_game since maps2's rebalance 96ada1a8f9: (1) the re-plan runs at findPath's DEFAULT node cap in a loop of up to TAP_PROVE_TRIES+1 = 5 searches, each but the last followed by proveRoute simulating ROUTE_PROVE_STEPS = 60 frames of stepAutopilot — bounded only by TAP_PROVE_BUDGET_MS = 16 ms, which is a sane budget for ONE player tap and a heavy one per stalling monster per stall; (2) findPath defaults canSwim TRUE (index.ts:3652), so a land monster's replacement route can cross water it can never walk: it reaches the shore, makeBlockedElev refuses every step, netStalled (ROUTE_NET_WU 16 wu in ROUTE_NET_MS 1000) fires again a second later, another 16 ms goes, and after ROUTE_REPLANS it stands still for the random pause — 'walking on the spot at a shoreline, then freezing, then repeating'. Also note `dithering` poisons the progress clock, so a monster being shoved by separationPush or arcing through monsterDodge cannot refresh it and is declared stalled. SUGGESTED, yours to judge: carry maxNodes and canSwim on AutopilotTrip (startTrip already receives both) and pass them to the re-plan's findPath; and give a server-side caller one budgeted re-plan instead of the walked proof loop (a roam leg is a wander, not a tap). RENDER3 RULE CHANGE (one rule set, tiles3.ts <-> render3.py): SLOPES ON BOTH SIDES OF A ONE-LEVEL RISE, the maintainer's 2026-09-24 ask ("almost always use slope tiles when the elevation change is only 1 level ... placed both to lower a level 2 to 1.5 and push up a level 1 to 1.5"). Shipped in games2 as the GAME rule (behind footBoundary, so the parity fixture keeps the any-higher bump until you carry it). The rule (tiles3.ts slopeHalfAt / slopeEligible / tiles3draw slopeLift + slopeTopOnly): (1) a cell is ELIGIBLE when its ground has an approved slope set, its whole 8-ring is that ground, and its exact-one mask equals its any-higher mask (no corner raised only by cells two or more up). (2) An eligible cell RAISES every corner a cell exactly one up touches (the bump's own mask) and its tile is drawn `elevation` rows UP — the published sets draw their plateau on the library diamond and the flat part SUNK `elevation` rows below it (tile 15 tops the frame at row 0, tile 0 at row 4), so drawn at the level the raise sank the cell 4 px, which is what render3 does today. (3) An eligible cell CUTS a corner when every cell touching it is eligible, the corner holds exactly its level and the one below, and every same-level cell there raises nothing: its tile index = the corners that stay, drawn AT the level, so the lowered corners sink over the wall. A cell that raises anything cuts nothing. (4) Top-only mask = the library diamond extended `elevation` rows DOWN (the sunk part and the lip's face lie under the silhouette). Measured on the_game: 403 raises, 209 cuts, every cut corner has a raise under it, no two same-level plates disagree on a corner (server/test/slopes.test.ts). Docs: games2/docs/tiles3-rendering.md "A ONE-LEVEL RISE WEARS HIS SLOPE ON BOTH SIDES".
